root_cause.text: The AF_UNIX `unix_ioctl()` implementation handled `SIOCATMARK` for all socket types and only checked the receive queue, even though urgent-mark/OOB semantics exist only for `SOCK_STREAM`, causing `SOCK_DGRAM` and `SOCK_SEQPACKET` sockets to incorrectly accept an unsupported ioctl instead of returning `-EOPNOTSUPP`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (sk->sk_type != SOCK_STREAM) return -EOPNOTSUPP;` before `skb_peek(&sk->sk_receive_queue);`, and the CVE description states that in AF_UNIX “MSG_OOB is supported only for SOCK_STREAM sockets” while `SOCK_DGRAM` and `SOCK_SEQPACKET` “should not support SIOCATMARK either.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject unsupported unix ioctl handling on non-stream sockets by returning -EOPNOTSUPP early.
intent_record.what: A check was added at the start of the ioctl handling path to immediately return -EOPNOTSUPP if the socket type is not SOCK_STREAM, before taking u->iolock and accessing the receive queue.
intent_record.how: This prevents the ioctl logic from running on non-stream Unix sockets, avoiding unsupported operations on socket types that do not satisfy the assumptions of the code that follows.

Because the code proceeded for all AF_UNIX socket types without first rejecting non-SOCK_STREAM sockets, it allowed unsupported ioctl handling on SOCK_DGRAM and SOCK_SEQPACKET instead of returning -EOPNOTSUPP.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is part of the pre-fix SIOCATMARK path that only inspects the receive queue. Because it was reached for all AF_UNIX socket types without first rejecting non-SOCK_STREAM sockets, SOCK_DGRAM and SOCK_SEQPACKET incorrectly accepted the ioctl instead of returning -EOPNOTSUPP.

commit 314001f0bf927015e459c9d387d62a231fe93af3
Author: Rao Shoaib <rao.shoaib@oracle.com>
Date:   Sun Aug 1 00:57:07 2021 -0700

    af_unix: Add OOB support
    
    This patch adds OOB support for AF_UNIX sockets.
    The semantics is same as TCP.
    
    The last byte of a message with the OOB flag is
    treated as the OOB byte. The byte is separated into
    a skb and a pointer to the skb is stored in unix_sock.
    The pointer is used to enforce OOB semantics.
    
    Signed-off-by: Rao
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described is the old AF_UNIX `unix_ioctl()` handling of `SIOCATMARK` for all socket types with only receive-queue checks. In this snippet, `SIOCATMARK` is added only under `#if IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_AF_UNIX_OOB)` and the code checks OOB state explicitly: `skb = skb_peek(&sk->sk_receive_queue); if (skb && skb == u->oob_skb) answ = 1;`. Because this commit is adding OOB support, the prior bug is not present here as a wrong unconditional ioctl implementation; instead, the code already contains the OOB-aware handling. The snippet is sufficient to determine that the vulnerable construct is absent and the fix is present in this version.
